name: Barcodes Talk
summary: Authentic UPC and EAN barcodes for retail and Amazon listings. Buy GS1-sourced barcodes for your products as a one-time purchase, without an annual GS1 membership.
best_for: sellers and small brands listing on marketplaces or in independent retail who want authentic, one-time-cost UPC/EAN barcodes without an annual GS1 membership
skip_if: your target retailer or brand registry explicitly requires a GS1-issued company prefix in your own name — then buy direct from GS1
honest_knock: The honest caveat is about fit, not the codes. Some large retailers and brand registries — notably certain Amazon Brand Registry and big-box requirements — increasingly ask for a GS1-issued prefix tied to your own company, and a third-party barcode (legitimate and globally unique as it is) may not satisfy that specific gatekeeping. For most marketplaces and independent retail it's completely fine and far cheaper; just confirm your channel's exact requirement first.

pricing.notes: (prices re-verified 2026-09-19 on barcodestalk.com/buy-barcodes) One-off purchase, no subscription and no renewal. The full published ladder runs eighteen rungs: 1 barcode $5.00; 5 for $10.00 ($2.00 each); 10 for $15.00 ($1.50); 25 for $25.00 ($1.00); 50 for $35.00 ($0.70); 100 for $45.00 ($0.45); 200 for $80.00 ($0.40); 500 for $125.00 ($0.25); 1,000 for $180.00 ($0.18); 1,500 for $225.00 ($0.15); 2,000 for $260.00 ($0.13); 2,500 for $300.00 ($0.12); 5,000 for $500.00 ($0.10); 10,000 for $650.00 ($0.065); 25,000 for $1,200.00 ($0.048); 50,000 for $2,300.00 ($0.046); 75,000 for $3,225.00 ($0.043); and 100,000 for $3,500.00 ($0.035). Larger quantities are quote-only. The unit price drops fastest between one and a hundred codes. Every purchase includes both UPC and EAN formats, high-resolution EPS and JPEG images, a Certificate of GTIN Assignment, Excel and PDF spreadsheets of the assigned numbers, instant download, and the vendor's Works for Amazon Guarantee. Unchanged from our 5 September reading.

compare_with.why: GS1 costs more and can carry ongoing fees, but it's the only route when a channel demands a prefix registered to your company
